# EMPIRIC TREATMENT: VENTILATOR ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA (VAP)

Pneumonia occurring 48 hours or more after endotracheal intubation

---

References:

- Kalil AC et al. Clin Infect Dis 2016. 63:1.
- Pugh R. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2015 Aug 24:2015(8):CD00757
- Daghmouri MA. EClinicalMedicine. 2023 1:58:101880
- Dennesen PJ. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2001. 163:1371.
- Luna CM. Crit Care Med 2003. 31:676.
- Up-to-date website
Therapy:
## Empiric Treatment (see below for multidrug resistance (MDR))

Obtain MRSA nasal PCR and sputum culture before antibiotics, whenever possible.

Narrow therapy based on results of culture and susceptibility tests. Discontinue MRSA and/or Pseudomonas coverage if not isolated from respiratory cultures.

Discontinue MRSA coverage if MRSA nasal PCR negative.

[Re-evaluate Nosocomial pneumonia at 72 hours](nosocomial-pneumonia-re-evaluation-at-72-hours)

Preferred:

See below for history of Gram-negative resistance to preferred antimicrobials
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R  for 7 days

<OR>
Piperacillin-tazo 4.5gm IV q8h ext inf [R] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h [R]
for 7 days
History of Gram-negative resistance to cefepime and piperacillin-tazobactam within the last year:

Meropenem 1 gm IV q8h R <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h R for 7 days

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h [R,O]
History of MRSA infection/colonization or clinically unstable (e.g ., intubation, hypotension)
< ADD > Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q 12 hours ($) [R]

## MDR gram-negative/high severity of illness and MDR risks

Prior intravenous antibiotic use within 90 days (especially broad spectrum)

Septic shock at the time of VAP

ARDS preceding VAP
5 or more days of hospitalization prior to the occurrence of VAP Acute renal replacement therapy prior to VAP onset
<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV once R,O to one of the regimens above
